instructions.title: How to use the YAML to JSON Converter

steps.title: Paste your YAML or JSON input
steps.description: Paste your YAML or JSON into the input area. You can also upload a .yaml, .yml, or .json file. The tool auto-detects whether your input is YAML or JSON and sets the conversion direction automatically.

steps.title: Select conversion direction and options
steps.description: Choose the conversion direction — YAML → JSON or JSON → YAML — using the toggle buttons at the top. Adjust output indentation (2 or 4 spaces) if needed. Options take effect immediately on the current input.

steps.title: Review real-time conversion and validation
steps.description: Conversion happens in real time as you type. Syntax errors appear inline with descriptive messages. A status indicator shows whether your document is valid. For YAML multi-document files (separated by ---), each document is converted independently.

steps.title: Copy or download the converted output
steps.description: Click 'Copy' to copy the converted output to your clipboard, or 'Download' to save it as a file with the correct extension (.yaml or .json). Paste directly into your Kubernetes manifest, Docker Compose, or GitHub Actions workflow file.

steps.title: Use advanced features: anchors, TypeScript export
steps.description: YAML anchors (&name) and aliases (*name) are automatically resolved in the JSON output. Merge keys (<<:) expand correctly. Use the TypeScript and JSON Schema export buttons to generate type definitions from your converted structures.

proTips: Kubernetes YAML requires correct indentation — use real-time validation before applying manifests with kubectl
YAML anchors must be defined before aliases in the same document or conversion will fail
JSON doesn't support comments: YAML comments are stripped in output — check the warning indicator
For Docker Compose port values, verify numbers aren't converted to strings in JSON output
Multi-document YAML (---) converts to a JSON array — access the correct index in your code
Use the TypeScript export to automatically generate type interfaces from config file structures
troubleshooting: Indentation error: YAML requires spaces, not tabs — check for tab characters in your input
Unresolved anchor: ensure the anchor (&name) is defined before the alias (*name) in the document
Comments lost: YAML comments (#) are not supported in JSON and are removed automatically
Wrong types in JSON: YAML interprets '1.0' as a number — wrap in quotes to keep it as a string
Multi-document result: the JSON output is an array — use the correct index in your application
Large file performance: for files over 1MB, conversion may take a few seconds
